title: Iki environment (iki/v1)
description: What a plugin's actions need to run, wherever they run: software, the smallest machine, and data volumes. Each deployment binds it to its own compute templates.

apiVersion.description: The spec version this manifest follows.

name.description: The environment's name in kebab-case, such as `alphafold-gpu`, which its actions give in `runs_on.environment`.

tiers.description: The compute tiers it can run on.

labels.description: What a self-hosted machine must have to run it, such as `chromeleon` for the software or `gpu`: a self-hosted run goes only to a machine with every one of them (ADR 0112). Name what it needs, not where: a deployment adds its own in its binding. Only for an environment on the self-hosted tier.

resources.description: The smallest machine its actions run on.

image.description: The container image with its registry, pinned by its digest (`ghcr.io/acme/alphafold@sha256:…`). The container and vm tiers run it, and so does the self-hosted tier on machines with Docker or Podman.

customer_image_required.description: This environment's container- or vm-tier image comes from an EnvironmentImageBinding in the deployment's compute.yaml.

python.description: A Python virtual environment, for the backend and self-hosted tiers.

requirements.description: A requirements file in the plugin, every package pinned with `==` and its `--hash`, as `uv pip compile --generate-hashes` writes it.

iki_runtime.description: Install the plugin runtime (`iki_runtime`: readers for compressed text, FASTQ, AIRR files and HELM) that this Iki release ships: `true`, or `{ helm: true }` for its HELM reader too. Its version is part of the environment's build, so an upgrade that changes it rebuilds the environment. Leave it out of the requirements file.

conda.description: A conda environment, for the backend and self-hosted tiers.

lockfile.description: An explicit lockfile in the plugin, every package with its hash, as `conda-lock` or `conda list --explicit --md5` writes it.

iki_runtime.description: Install the plugin runtime (`iki_runtime`) that this Iki release ships into the environment's Python, which the lockfile must include: `true`, or `{ helm: true }` for its HELM reader too. Its version is part of the environment's build.

volumes.description: Data volumes its actions read, such as reference databases, by name.

setup.description: A script that fills its volumes once, when the environment is built. Its runs are recorded as data versions.

script.description: The script that fills the volumes: a path in the plugin, relative to its root.

timeout.description: The longest the setup may take before it's stopped. 6h unless given.

requires_approval.description: A compute admin approves each build before it starts, for setups that cost a lot.

network.description: The hosts the setup may download from.

oneOf.description: The plugin runtime, with the readers that need more than Python's standard library.

helm.description: `iki_runtime.helm`: HELM read by iki-wasm, Iki's own reader. The environment gets this Iki release's iki-wasm module, whose SHA-256 is part of its build too; its requirements must pin `wasmtime`.

label.description: A label, such as `chromeleon`, `gpu` or `lab-3`: lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, starting and ending with a letter or digit.

name.description: A name in kebab-case, such as `alphafold-gpu`.

file.description: A path in the plugin, relative to its root.

quantity.description: An amount of memory or disk, such as `512Mi`, `64Gi` or `3Ti`.

memory.description: The memory a run needs, such as `8Gi`.

gpu.description: The GPUs a run needs. Backend workers have none: use the self-hosted, container or vm tier.

min_memory.description: The memory each GPU must have.

scratch_disk.description: Local disk for the run's working files.

volume.description: One data volume: its size, where runs see it, how it's read, and what fills it.

size.description: How big the volume is, such as `500Gi`.

access.description: `read_only_many` (the default): many runs read it at once. `read_write_once`: one run at a time may change it.

performance.description: What the data needs from the disk: `standard` (the default), `high_iops` for many small reads, or `high_throughput` for large ones.

mount.description: Where runs see it: an absolute path.
